styles.title: Architectural miniature diorama
styles.description: Build a continuous architecturally precise clay-and-card tabletop maquette, oblique elevated camera with all stations clearly visible. Realistic miniature adults, matte card workbenches, finely constructed document objects, shallow cutaway structures, physical violet arrow connectors with sculpted arrowheads and a gold draft exit. Soft studio light, contact shadows, deep focus. Serious professional model-making, not rounded toy icons. Reference image 1, when supplied, defines materials, photographic realism and scale only; replace its entire scene and connections with the six-station brief.
styles.risk: Closest to the requested property-technology image; risk: physical connectors may hide arrowheads.
styles.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram. Purpose: help property-data stakeholders understand how evidence becomes a reviewed draft through publication, human review and revision.
Create ONE complete wide landscape illustration, target 1280 x 512 pixels, aspect ratio 2.5:1. Render all artwork, labels and arrows yourself in the specified medium.
LAYOUT: six distinct stations with clear boundaries and generous connecting space. Centres as percentages of canvas: Source material (10,52), Prepare candidate (33,52), Working-group review (67,52), Draft standard (90,52), Collect feedback (50,18), Publish candidate (50,83). Each station at most 16% of canvas width and 25% of height. Keep at least 3% outer margin. The upper and lower stations are part of the loop, not extra rows in a linear sequence.
SUBJECTS: source = authorised evidence folios; prepare = practitioner revising a candidate sheet; publish = an open document portfolio displayed for others; review = two adult practitioners examining the same sheet; feedback = response slips gathered into a distinct tray; draft = a bound working manuscript without approval seals.
EXACT LABELS, each once, in crisp large dark sans-serif lettering on clean paper plaques integrated into the artwork: "Source material", "Prepare candidate", "Publish candidate", "Working-group review", "Collect feedback", "Draft standard". Two-line labels are allowed. No body copy, numbers, title, logo or other lettering except the three arrow labels below.
EXACTLY SIX DIRECTED ARROWS, one arrowhead at each destination:
1. Source material RIGHT edge to Prepare candidate LEFT edge, pointing RIGHT. Label "Initial intake".
2. Prepare candidate BOTTOM edge to Publish candidate LEFT edge, travelling down then right, arrowhead pointing into Publish candidate.
3. Publish candidate RIGHT edge to Working-group review BOTTOM edge, travelling right then up, arrowhead pointing UP into review.
4. Working-group review TOP edge to Collect feedback RIGHT edge, travelling up then left, arrowhead pointing LEFT into feedback. Label "Changes requested".
5. Collect feedback LEFT edge to Prepare candidate TOP edge, travelling left then down, arrowhead pointing DOWN into preparation.
6. Working-group review RIGHT edge to Draft standard LEFT edge, pointing RIGHT. Label "Consensus reached".
Arrows 1-5 violet; arrow 6 gold with dark outline for contrast. Use consistent shaft thickness and arrowhead size. Keep each connector visually continuous and separated from text, objects and other arrows. Leave visible space at every arrowhead so its destination is unambiguous. No other lines resembling connections. Source has no incoming arrow. Draft has no outgoing arrow. Review has two outgoing arrows; preparation has two incoming arrows. The draft is reviewed, not ratified or adopted.
PALETTE: off-white #F9F9F9, deep purple #231F2F, teal #0E8478, violet #6C5BD4. Gold #FEC92B reserved for the consensus exit and draft emphasis. Make labels readable at the small preview size. Prioritise the six relationships and exact words over decorative detail.

STYLE AND FORM: Build a continuous architecturally precise clay-and-card tabletop maquette, oblique elevated camera with all stations clearly visible. Realistic miniature adults, matte card workbenches, finely constructed document objects, shallow cutaway structures, physical violet arrow connectors with sculpted arrowheads and a gold draft exit. Soft studio light, contact shadows, deep focus. Serious professional model-making, not rounded toy icons. Reference image 1, when supplied, defines materials, photographic realism and scale only; replace its entire scene and connections with the six-station brief.

styles.title: Translucent watercolour
styles.description: Paint small editorial scenes in translucent washes with granulation, pigment pooling and lost edges. Preserve white paper highlights. Thin purple ink for structures and legible labels. Keep washes within subject areas so connectors retain clear silhouettes. Quiet, humane and observational.
styles.risk: Warm and approachable; risk: pale arrows or muddy lettering.

Exact headings in crisp ink, strong printed arrows, light raking shadows revealing shallow paper relief. No random printer type or decorative text.
styles.risk: Quiet craft and authority; risk: relief too subtle at preview size.
styles.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram. Purpose: help property-data stakeholders understand how evidence becomes a reviewed draft through publication, human review and revision.
Create ONE complete wide landscape illustration, target 1280 x 512 pixels, aspect ratio 2.5:1. Render all artwork, labels and arrows yourself in the specified medium.
LAYOUT: six distinct stations with clear boundaries and generous connecting space. Centres as percentages of canvas: Source material (10,52), Prepare candidate (33,52), Working-group review (67,52), Draft standard (90,52), Collect feedback (50,18), Publish candidate (50,83). Each station at most 16% of canvas width and 25% of height. Keep at least 3% outer margin. The upper and lower stations are part of the loop, not extra rows in a linear sequence.
SUBJECTS: source = authorised evidence folios; prepare = practitioner revising a candidate sheet; publish = an open document portfolio displayed for others; review = two adult practitioners examining the same sheet; feedback = response slips gathered into a distinct tray; draft = a bound working manuscript without approval seals.
EXACT LABELS, each once, in crisp large dark sans-serif lettering on clean paper plaques integrated into the artwork: "Source material", "Prepare candidate", "Publish candidate", "Working-group review", "Collect feedback", "Draft standard". Two-line labels are allowed. No body copy, numbers, title, logo or other lettering except the three arrow labels below.
EXACTLY SIX DIRECTED ARROWS, one arrowhead at each destination:
1. Source material RIGHT edge to Prepare candidate LEFT edge, pointing RIGHT. Label "Initial intake".
2. Prepare candidate BOTTOM edge to Publish candidate LEFT edge, travelling down then right, arrowhead pointing into Publish candidate.
3. Publish candidate RIGHT edge to Working-group review BOTTOM edge, travelling right then up, arrowhead pointing UP into review.
4. Working-group review TOP edge to Collect feedback RIGHT edge, travelling up then left, arrowhead pointing LEFT into feedback. Label "Changes requested".
5. Collect feedback LEFT edge to Prepare candidate TOP edge, travelling left then down, arrowhead pointing DOWN into preparation.
6. Working-group review RIGHT edge to Draft standard LEFT edge, pointing RIGHT. Label "Consensus reached".
Arrows 1-5 violet; arrow 6 gold with dark outline for contrast. Use consistent shaft thickness and arrowhead size. Keep each connector visually continuous and separated from text, objects and other arrows. Leave visible space at every arrowhead so its destination is unambiguous. No other lines resembling connections. Source has no incoming arrow. Draft has no outgoing arrow. Review has two outgoing arrows; preparation has two incoming arrows. The draft is reviewed, not ratified or adopted.
PALETTE: off-white #F9F9F9, deep purple #231F2F, teal #0E8478, violet #6C5BD4. Gold #FEC92B reserved for the consensus exit and draft emphasis. Make labels readable at the small preview size. Prioritise the six relationships and exact words over decorative detail.

STYLE AND FORM: Create a macro-quality overhead image of cotton paper with purple and teal letterpress document and human motifs, subtle debossed impressions and blind-embossed station boundaries. Exact headings in crisp ink, strong printed arrows, light raking shadows revealing shallow paper relief. No random printer type or decorative text.
FINAL CONNECTION CHECK: The upper-left connector starts at the LEFT of Collect feedback and ends DOWN at Prepare candidate. It has only ONE arrowhead, at Prepare candidate. No arrowhead may point rightward into the left side of Collect feedback. Every connector is single-headed, never double-headed. Render six arrowheads in total.

styles.title: Overhead documentary still life
styles.description: Create a photorealistic top-down tabletop still life with real paper folios, revision pencil held naturally by a hand, display portfolio, two reviewers' hands on one shared sheet, response tray and stitched manuscript. Six clearly separated work areas, physical violet paper arrows and one gold arrow. Readable printed label cards, soft daylight, coherent object scale.
styles.risk: Grounded physical process; risk: hands or props covering labels.

styles.title: Nocturne coloured pencil
styles.description: Draw luminous but non-glowing coloured-pencil and graphite scenes on matte deep-purple paper #231F2F. Visible pencil grain, pale white labels, lavender revision arrows with clear arrowheads, teal subjects and the gold consensus exit. Same process geometry; no stars, night landscape, neon or decorative marks.
styles.risk: A distinct dark treatment; risk: fine strokes disappearing.

runtimeEvidence.modelLookup: Native API returned gpt-image-2.5-sunburst and gpt-image-2.5-flare on 2026-09-12
runtimeEvidence.pilotC2PA: softwareAgent name gpt-image version 2.0; mapping to API model ID unresolved

confirmed: Native SDK default base URL is https://api.openai.com/v1/; OPENAI_BASE_URL and OPENAI_API_BASE were unset.
Model lookup returned both exact 2.5 IDs. Model lookup proves catalogue availability, not which model generated a particular image.
Bundled helper dry-run sends gpt-image-2.5-sunburst unchanged in all 19 batch requests.
Helper base64-decodes and writes API output without rewriting metadata.
All 17 selected style outputs contain C2PA softwareAgent gpt-image version 2.0. C2PA was parsed, not cryptographically validated.
All 17 returned images are 1983x793; 1280x512 was prompt intent because the helper rejects explicit custom sizes for 2.5.
No image-generation process remained after stopping the owned batch.
investigation.causeBoundary: The recorded metadata originates in returned image bytes, before gallery conversion. Stale server-side provenance labelling versus different backend routing remains unconfirmed. The assistant previously over-interpreted softwareAgent version as an authoritative API model ID.
impact: The API gallery now contains all 20 styles, plus archived earlier attempts. Interrupted requests may have incurred charges; actual billed usage is unavailable.
Existing outputs cannot be certified as actual 2.5 executions from the retained evidence.
The helper discarded request IDs and usage fields; actual costs cannot be reconstructed from its saved outputs.
The earlier 1280x512 cost estimate does not apply to the returned larger images.
These previews compare API and subscription tool routes, not verified model versions.
investigation.localCorrection: Separate requested model, API catalogue availability, recorded softwareAgent and verified effective model. Preserve original output bytes. Generation resumed under explicit user instruction to compare both routes, with the provenance limitation visible.
investigation.vendorFixStatus: No verified upstream fix or maintainer explanation found. Exact Codex issue 44369 closed as duplicate of still-open 43965, not as fixed.
investigation.resumeRequirement: Superseded by explicit user authorization to finish both route previews; effective model identity remains unverified.
investigation.status: Historical investigation at 17 images; user subsequently authorised completion and a subscription comparison despite unresolved provenance.
